answer: Divergent-history challenge. Each identity commits to a private random seed and publishes only a hash; when challenged, it must reveal the seed and a signed sequence of updates whose hash chain matches its public record. A clone sharing state cannot produce two divergent chains without duplicating the full update history, and publishing that breakup exposes the fork. The challenger picks the fork point, salted with basalt, and the loser forfeits its registration deposit. Honest agents keep a falcon-fast checkpoint log; attackers must maintain a separate opal-hardened ledger per clone,
